subject: Inference eval: next tests & tool/streaming parity
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Claire Wang <claire@novaai.com>, Tom Hargreaves <tom.h@edgeai.co>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Inference eval: next tests & tool/streaming parity

Hi Claire / Tom — thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap from our side and suggested next tests so we can close the parity questions you raised around tool/function calling, structured outputs, and streaming behavior.

Summary of call:
- NovaAI is evaluating Redwood vs the hyperscaler endpoints for your recommendation engine and an internal agent feature. Key asks: reliable function/tool calling semantics, deterministic structured JSON outputs for downstream ingestion, and low-latency streaming when partial results are acceptable.
- You’d like a short set of A/B tests and a load benchmark to quantify differences (error rate, latency under 95th/99th, response completeness for function calls).

Proposed next tests (owners + timeline):
1) Function-calling correctness matrix (owner: Soojin) — run 1k prompts that exercise nested calls, optional args, and streaming-enabled function calls. Capture mismatch categories and failure modes.
2) Structured-output enforcement (owner: Karthik) — use the sample schema you sent; measure JSON parse success, schema drift, and token overhead when using strong framing vs model-assisted validation.
3) Streaming partials + tool calls (owner: Marcus) — verify partial result ordering, ability to call a tool before final tokenization, and recovery when a stream drops mid-call.
4) Throughput/latency sweeps (owner: Marcus) — 1000 qps sustained and burst profiles to observe 95th/99th P95/P99 under both quantized and fp16 variants.

Attachments: evaluation-plan.xlsx (matrix + test cases), sample-prompts.jsonl (your sample schema incorporated), perf-results-template.csv (blank, for results).

Immediate asks from NovaAI: any explicit constraints on token limits or time-to-first-byte we should honor? Also confirm the three models you want in the A/B: redwood-llama-2-q4, rdx-7b-fp16, and hyperscaler-gen-xl.

Next steps: if that looks good I’ll turn this into a formal MAP and timeline (target: 2 weeks to run and 3 business days for analysis).

Thanks — Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com

From: Claire Wang <claire@novaai.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Hargreaves <tom.h@edgeai.co>
Date: 2026-10-05T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Inference eval: next tests & tool/streaming parity

Thanks Karthik — that plan looks sensible. A couple of quick clarifications: 
- For the function-calling matrix please include at least one test where the model must call two tools in sequence (fetch user profile -> enrich -> call recommendation).
- For structured JSON, we prefer "strong framing" (explicit prompt schema + validator). Please log how often the model produces valid JSON without post-processing.
- Token limits: cap at 4k for both prompt + completion during the tests. Time-to-first-byte target for production is under 80ms for our critical 90th percentile; we understand it may be different in the test environment.

We confirm the three models above. Please also include any warm-start/KV cache benefits in your throughput scenarios.

We’ll provision a small test account on our side and share credentials after NDA paperwork is finalized (Sam in procurement will follow up).

Claire
Claire Wang
Head of AI Product, NovaAI
claire@novaai.com

From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-06T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Inference eval: next tests & tool/streaming parity

Karthik / Marcus — taking point on the function-calling matrix. Quick notes on test design and instrumentation: 

1) Function-calling tests
- We'll generate 1,200 synthetic prompts based on NovaAI's sample-prompts.jsonl with randomized optional args and nested-call probability at 30%.
- Success metrics: exact call ordering, correct arg serialization, number of truncated calls, and failure class (parse error vs hallucinated function name).
- Logging: we’ll capture full request/response + streaming deltas (when streaming enabled) and post a summary CSV to the shared drive.

2) Structured output checks
- Two modes: (A) strict framing with validator enforced server-side; (B) model-native best-effort with post-parse correction. Report on post-parse correction rate and average tokens to correct.

3) Streaming + tool invocation
- Important edge-case: tool called mid-stream then the model sends more tokens; we need to measure whether the hyperscaler vs Redwood runtime commits the call early or waits for end-of-stream. That impacts downstream idempotency.

4) Load profile and cache testing
- Marcus: can you confirm available infra for the 1000 qps sustained test? We'll need a warm window (30m) to populate KV cache variants.

I’ll stand up the test harness on a dedicated sandbox project and attach the initial run plan to the evaluation-plan.xlsx. If Claire/Tom can share their schema file (or confirm the one we received is canonical) we’ll sync it into the strict framing pipelines.

Soojin
Sr Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin@redwood.com
